atoms.b: As a result of changes in heat and pressure, rocks within the Earth’s crust can become ((++molten solid)).
Molten rock under the ground is called ((++magma silt)) and molten rock above ground is called ((++lava sand)).
((++Igneous_rocks Sedimentary_rocks)) are formed when magma or lava ((++cools melts)) and ((++solidifies liquifies)).

instruction.text: Select true or false for the following statements.

atoms.a: Igneous rocks are typically hard rocks.

hint.text: If a rock is permeable, it lets water through it easily.

atoms.a: Igneous rocks are worn away easily by the weather.
Some igneous rocks can be glossy.

feedback.correct: One example of a glossy igneous rock is obsidian.
